subject: Chemistry
scope: AQA 7405 AS 3.1.3.2 and 3.1.3.4, mock-eligible representation and crystal-structure diagram recall; diagram execution requires original exam-style questions

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: How is a single covalent bond shown in a displayed structural formula?
cards.back: As one line between the two bonded atoms.
accept: As one line between the two bonded atoms.
One line between the bonded atoms.
Draw a single line connecting the bonded atoms.
Use a line between the atoms.
reject: As a pair of opposite ions.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: For a sketch of solid sodium chloride, what arrangement and charges must be represented?
cards.back: A repeating lattice of alternating Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions, with their charges shown.
accept: A repeating lattice of alternating Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions, with their charges shown.
An alternating repeating lattice of Na+ and Cl- ions.
Alternating positive sodium and negative chloride ions arranged in a lattice.
A giant lattice with alternating Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions.
reject: A sea of delocalised electrons surrounding sodium atoms.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What should a metallic bonding diagram for solid magnesium show?
cards.back: Positive Mg²⁺ ions in a lattice with delocalised electrons between them.
accept: Positive Mg²⁺ ions in a lattice with delocalised electrons between them.
Mg2+ ions in a regular lattice surrounded by delocalised electrons.
Positive magnesium ions with a sea of mobile delocalised electrons.
A regular array of Mg²⁺ ions and delocalised electrons.
reject: Separate magnesium molecules joined by weak forces.
Fixed negative magnesium ions surrounded by protons.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: In a diamond structure diagram, how many other carbon atoms must each carbon bond to, and how?
cards.back: Four others by strong covalent bonds in a three-dimensional tetrahedral network.
accept: Four others by strong covalent bonds in a three-dimensional tetrahedral network.
Four other carbons in a tetrahedral network.
Four carbon neighbours joined by covalent bonds in three dimensions.
Each carbon bonds to four other carbons.
reject: Three carbon neighbours in flat hexagonal layers.
Carbon atoms held together only by intermolecular forces.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What features distinguish a graphite structure drawing from a diamond structure drawing?
cards.back: Hexagonal layers, each carbon covalently bonded to three others, with delocalised electrons.
accept: Hexagonal layers, each carbon covalently bonded to three others, with delocalised electrons.
Hexagonal sheets with each carbon bonded to three others and delocalised electrons.
Layers of hexagons, each C makes three covalent bonds with one delocalised electron.
Three bonds per carbon in layers containing delocalised electrons.
reject: Four covalent bonds from each carbon in a 3D tetrahedral network.
Separate I2 molecules held by intermolecular attractions.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: When showing ice, what is the distinction between O–H bonds and hydrogen bonds?
cards.back: Solid O–H covalent bonds are within water molecules; dashed hydrogen bonds are between molecules.
accept: Solid O–H covalent bonds are within water molecules; dashed hydrogen bonds are between molecules.
O-H bonds are covalent within H2O; dashed hydrogen bonds link different water molecules.
Covalent O–H bonds stay within molecules and intermolecular H-bonds are drawn dashed.
Draw solid O-H bonds within each water molecule and dashed hydrogen bonds between water molecules.
reject: Dashed O-H covalent bonds are between different molecules.
The O-H covalent bonds break and are replaced by ionic bonds.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: How should an iodine crystal be represented in a bonding diagram?
cards.back: As separate I₂ molecules with weak intermolecular induced dipole–dipole forces between them.
accept: As separate I₂ molecules with weak intermolecular induced dipole–dipole forces between them.
Separate I2 molecules held by London dispersion forces.
Discrete I2 molecules with induced dipole attractions between molecules.
Iodine consists of separate diatomic molecules linked by weak intermolecular forces.
reject: A giant covalent network of individual iodine atoms.
I2 molecules joined by new strong I-I covalent bonds across the crystal.
